senses.definition: (intransitive) To move slowly with the abdomen close to the ground.
examples: Lizards and snakes crept over the ground.

quotes.text: One evening, while the Rabbit was lying there alone, watching the ants that ran to and fro between his velvet paws in the grass, he saw two strange beings creep out of the tall bracken near him.

Reed tips face the dawn
shivering in the autumn wind
At P'u-k'ou the winter tide
has not yet come
Sunrise on the sandy bank
pocked with narrow caves
Pale frogs and dark crabs
creep without end.

senses.definition: (intransitive, of plants) To grow across a surface rather than upwards.
(intransitive) To move slowly and quietly in a particular direction.
examples: He tried to creep past the guard without being seen.

quotes.text: Electrification of the Eastern Region main line from Strasbourg, incidentally, is steadily creeping nearer to Paris, and is now complete as far as Château Thierry, 59 miles away; [...].

senses.definition: (intransitive) To make small gradual changes, usually in a particular direction.
examples: Prices have been creeping up all year.

senses.definition: (idiomatic) To move in a stealthy or secret manner; to move imperceptibly or clandestinely; to insinuate itself or oneself.

quotes.text: […]guard his understanding from being imposed on by the willful or at least undesigned sophistry which creeps into most of the books of argument.

senses.definition: To slip, or to become slightly displaced.
examples: The collodion on a negative, or a coat of varnish, may creep in drying.
The quicksilver on a mirror may creep.

senses.definition: To move or behave with servility or exaggerated humility; to fawn.

quotes.text: To come as humbly as they used to creep / To holy altars.

senses.definition: To have a sensation as of insects creeping on the skin of the body; to crawl.
examples: The sight made my flesh creep.

senses.definition: The movement of something that creeps (like worms or snails).
A relatively small gradual change, variation or deviation (from a planned value) in a measure.
A slight displacement of an object; the slight movement of something.
(uncountable) The gradual expansion or proliferation of something beyond its original goals or boundaries, considered negatively.
(publishing) In sewn books, the tendency of pages on the inside of a quire to stand out farther than those on the outside of it.
(materials science) An increase in strain with time; the gradual flow or deformation of a material under stress.
(geology) The imperceptible downslope movement of surface rock.
(informal, derogatory) Someone creepy (annoyingly unpleasant), especially one who is strange or eccentric.
